subject: Incident: temporary APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@acme-retail.com>, api-ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:12:00Z
Subject: Incident: APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups

Hi Samuel / Acme ops team,

Quick update and immediate actions — we observed a control-plane disruption affecting a subset of APAC and US-East edge POPs that began at ~14:48 UTC. Symptoms you reported (failed initial handshakes and spikes in 5xx) match our telemetry. Engineering has flagged this as a regional routing degradation and we have an ETA for mitigations, but I want to give you actionable steps to keep traffic healthy while we stabilize.

Immediate options for your team (pick one):
- Option A — Regional header override (fastest): add HTTP header X-Redwood-Region: eu to force EU routing for the next 2–6 hours. This will keep requests to EU endpoints and avoid the affected edges.
- Option B — Use multi-region endpoint: switch to api.multi.redwood.ai for transparent failover. This is a simple DNS change and will route traffic to the nearest healthy region automatically.
- Option C — Redirect at load balancer: update your L4 routing to send traffic to our eu-west egress IP range (see reroute-quick-checklist.txt attached).

Notes: requests routed to EU will be served from EU infrastructure; we will not move data to a non-EU location if your account is EU-resident — the routing override is a regional preference, not data residency override.

I attached a short checklist to make the switch quick and the incident timeline so you can correlate. Please confirm which option you prefer; if you want us to make temporary policy adjustments on your behalf we can (we'll need an explicit approval reply).

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Partner Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- reroute-quick-checklist.txt (plain text)
- inc-20260521-timeline.csv (csv)
From: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Incident: APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups

Thanks, Sofia — we saw the same errors just now. Two quick questions before we flip anything:
1) If we set X-Redwood-Region: eu, will session affinity / KV cache behave the same? We rely on local KV for short-lived prompts.
2) How long do you expect the regional blip to last? Do you have an ETA for restoring APAC / US edge POPs?

Prefer Option A for a quick test on 20% of traffic; we can ramp if stable. Can you confirm the exact header name and an example curl?

—Sam
Samuel Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail
api-ops@acme-retail.com

Subject: Re: Incident: APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups

Sofia / team —
On Fri, May 21, 2026 at 15:27 Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Sofia — we saw the same errors just now. Two quick questions before we flip anything:
> 1) If we set X-Redwood-Region: eu, will session affinity / KV cache behave the same? We rely on local KV for short-lived prompts.
> 2) How long do you expect the regional blip to last? Do you have an ETA for restoring APAC / US edge POPs?
>
> Prefer Option A for a quick test on 20% of traffic; we can ramp if stable. Can you confirm the exact header name and an example curl?

Short answers: 1) Yes — session affinity is preserved when you route to a region-backed endpoint. There is a short warm-up for the KV cache on first requests, but we preserve user-affinity tokens. 2) Engineering estimates 2–4 hours for full POP restoration but we'll provide updates.

Karthik — can you provide the exact header/curl snippet and a safe canary plan we can share with Acme? I will also pre-authorize a policy toggle (SLA exception) if needed to migrate Acme traffic to dedicated EU pods temporarily.

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Incident: APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups

Folks —
Forwarding the ops checklist and a safe canary we just validated in staging.

Canary plan (recommended):
- Step 0: Acquire approval (Sam or their ops lead replies to this thread).
- Step 1: Apply header override X-Redwood-Region: eu for 20% of requests via LB rule (duration 15m).
- Step 2: Monitor token error rate and 95th p99 latency for that slice. If error rate increases >1% relative to baseline, rollback immediately.
- Step 3: If stable for 30m, ramp to 50% for 30m, then 100% if stable.

Curl snippet:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu' \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"hello"}'

Operational notes for internal runbook:
- We will pre-seed KV cache on EU pods for Acme to reduce first-request tail latencies.
- If we need to move traffic for a customer on Dedicated, we can spin dedicated EU pods and migrate within 45m (SLA exception approved by Vanessa).

David — please stand by for pre-seed job; I will share the pod list in the next 10m.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident: APAC & US edge disruption — immediate routing guidance and follow-ups

Sam — thanks and appreciated.

We will proceed with Option A at 20% as you requested. Quick checklist (attached as reroute-quick-checklist.txt):
- Add header X-Redwood-Region: eu to 20% of traffic at LB (example curl above).
- Confirm monitoring window: 15m baseline, watch p95/p99 and token error ratio.
- If stable, ramp per Karthik's plan.

I also attached an initial postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.docx) — it's a placeholder that we'll update as we confirm root cause. Our status page will be updated here: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-05-21-apac-us-edge.

If you reply with a thumbs-up and the name of the engineer doing the LB change, we'll execute the canary and keep you updated every 15 minutes.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
